label: PF Backlog 626
title: Surface Gate 1.5/2.5 findings IN the Gate 1/Gate 2 review (store on item + gate sheet)

brief.what_adds: Store full findings on the item and render them in a Gate 1/Gate 2 review sheet
brief.problem: Findings only lived in an evidence file + a one-line summary; not guaranteed visible at the HIL gate

objective: Surface Gate 1.5/2.5 findings IN the Gate 1/Gate 2 review (store on item + gate sheet)
acceptance_criteria: Objective achieved: Surface Gate 1.5/2.5 findings IN the Gate 1/Gate 2 review (store on item + gate sheet)
in_scope: Surface Gate 1.5/2.5 findings IN the Gate 1/Gate 2 review (store on item + gate sheet)
approach: Surface Gate 1.5/2.5 findings IN the Gate 1/Gate 2 review (store on item + gate sheet)
verification: gate command renders Gate 1/2 sheet with findings inline; --apply stores findings on item; precheck PASS
evidence:
Gate 2.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=74bad6bf2558
BLOCKER:
  - New shipped logic (`review_block()`, `_latest_review()`, the `gate` subcommand, and the reworked `_ingest()` apply path) ships with zero test coverage. The operating standard — as applied to sibling item BI-PF-1429 in this same epic — treats missing tests for new shipped logic as a blocker. `scripts/dev/` Python is permitted by the language rule, but the test requirement is not waived.
MAJOR:
  - Acceptance criterion "store on item + **gate sheet**" is only half-delivered: `gate` prints the latest evidence block to stdout. There is no persisted gate-sheet artifact, and no change to precheck / `config/ci-cd-gates.json` / merge-gate wiring — so findings are surfaced "IN the Gate 1/Gate 2 review" only if a human manually runs the script. The objective as written is not achieved by the diff.
  - The `ingest` subcommand never gained `--mode`, so `_ingest()` defaults to `"diff"` — a Gate 1.5 (design) review can never be recorded through the ingest path. `run` supports mode; `ingest` does not. Inconsistent ingestion channel undermines the two-gate symmetry the item exists to create.
  - `_post_context()` now posts `verification` as a single-element list, replacing whatever was there. Observable integrity impact: BI-PF-1429's live item had its prior verification — which recorded 2 BLOCKERs on untested network/secret-handling code — overwritten with "precheck PASS …". Prior blocker evidence is erased from the item of record; only the JSONL history retains it. The gate sheet must be append/merge or keyed, not wholesale replace.
  - `_ingest --apply` appends a full rendered review block to `evidence` on every run with no dedup by `(sha, mode)`. Re-runs across SHAs accumulate unbounded, contradictory blocks in one list; there is no notion of "current" Gate 1.5/2.5 finding, which is precisely what a gate sheet needs.
  - The `gate` subcommand returns exit code `0` even when the rendered review contains BLOCKER findings (only missing-evidence returns `1`). The printed recommendation says "BLOCKED" but the process exit status says success — a trap the moment this is wired into CI.
  - BI-PF-1429 was closed with delivery recorded and verification rewritten to "precheck PASS (architect-review gate satisfied by evidence)" while its own review still carried 2 BLOCKERs (no tests for new secret/network path; config-declared `api_key_env`/`api_key_file` contract silently ignored). The epic's own gate discipline is being bypassed to close its own items — closure should be re-verified against the recorded blockers.
MINOR:
  - `_latest_review()` selects by filesystem `mtime`, which is not stable across fresh clones/CI checkouts (git does not preserve mtimes). "Latest review" can silently resolve to an arbitrary review; prefer an embedded timestamp or monotonic ordering in the evidence JSON.
  - Argparse now defines `--item` on both the parent parser and the `ing`/`gate` subparsers; behavior depends on subparser override semantics. Fragile and a maintenance trap.
  - `docs/BACKLOG-SUMMARY.md` was regenerated at 20:10, before BI-PF-1430 was created at 20:24 — the committed derived docs do not include the new item. Derived artifacts are being committed stale.
  - BI-PF-1430's body, acceptance criteria, in_scope, and approach are verbatim echoes of the title; the analysis itself flags "body/acceptance criteria thin" yet the item was auto-approved and marked ready. A change that touches gate integrity deserves a real AC (e.g., "findings visible in Gate 1/2 output AND persisted gate artifact AND enforced exit code").
NIT:
  - The `"1.5" if mode == "design" else "2.5"` mapping is duplicated in `review_block`, `_ingest`, and the `gate` branch; a single helper would remove the drift risk when Gate 3 arrives.
  - Several data files land without trailing newlines (`closed.json`, item JSONs, `counters.json`) — inconsistent POSIX text-file convention; will produce noisy diffs in some tooling.
  - Output is `print`-only; no structured event/log line for "gate review surfaced" — harder to observe adoption of the new gate path.
SUMMARY:
  - The change delivers a useful `review_block` renderer and a `gate` inspection subcommand, but the stated objective — findings surfaced IN the Gate 1/2 review with a persisted gate sheet — is not wired into any gate flow, and the ingest path cannot record design-mode reviews at all.
  - Top risks: (1) untested shipped logic per the project's own standard; (2) `verification`/`evidence` clobber-and-append semantics that erase and then bloat the item of record — observable now in BI-PF-1429, where recorded BLOCKERs were overwritten and the item closed; (3) exit-code semantics that would let a BLOCKED gate pass once automated.
  - Recommend: add tests, key findings by `(sha, mode)` with an explicit "current" pointer, make context updates merge rather than replace, thread `--mode` through ingest, return non-zero on blockers, and actually wire `gate` into the Gate 1/2 review path before claiming the AC.
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present

Gate 2.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=f91d60670c92
BLOCKER:
  - Acceptance criteria half-met: the AC is "store on item **+ gate sheet**". The diff persists findings to the item (evidence + verification) but nothing writes to a gate sheet anywhere — the new `gate` subcommand only prints to stdout and returns. Either the gate-sheet leg is missing entirely, or the design silently assumes an undocumented caller captures stdout, which is not a store.
  - `_post_context` now posts a new `{"evidence": [...], "verification": [...]}` shape with no shown API-side contract. If `/backlog/items/{id}/context` only appends/accepts `verification` (as the previous code assumed), the `evidence` payload — the exact deliverable of this AC — is silently dropped or, worse, replaces/appends the whole list, producing data duplication. The acceptance deliverable's persistence path is unverified.
MAJOR:
  - Review-sha exclusion broadened from `engineering/reviews/**` to `engineering/**`. Any non-derived, hand-authored content under `engineering/` (design docs, checklists, gate templates, anything else that lands there) no longer invalidates the review sha. That is a long-term integrity hole: source-of-truth changes can ship under a "passing" architect review. Exclusions should be explicitly whitelist-derived, not tree-wide.
  - `_latest_review` selects by `mode` + mtime only and never compares the stored `sha` to the current `diff_sha()`. The `gate` command will present findings from an older diff as if they were the current gate verdict — stale evidence masquerading as a live review. This is exactly the failure mode a "deterministic evidence gate" is supposed to prevent.
  - The `gate` subcommand returns 0 whenever any evidence exists, even when findings contain BLOCKERs (`_ingest` returns 1 in that case). A gate that is meant to be a hard rule (BI-PF-1428 lineage) must fail closed; printing "BLOCKED" while exiting success is an integrity break for any CI/pipeline consumer.
  - Evidence filename is `{item_id}-{sha}.json` and does not include `mode`. A design review and a diff review at the same sha silently overwrite one another (the new `mode` field implies the file is mode-scoped, but the key isn't). Data loss of prior evidence.
  - `_ingest(..., apply=True)` appends a fresh `review_block` to `item.evidence` on every run with no dedup/idempotency key (sha+mode). Re-running the ingest grows item context unboundedly and duplicates "latest" findings — maintainability and observability debt on the item record.
  - New shipped-facing logic (the `gate` enforcement path, recommendation computation, exit-code policy) is written as new Python in `scripts/dev/`. If this is invoked by the precheck/gate pipeline (hard rule), it is shipped logic and should be Go per the language rule; if it is purely a human dev tool, that boundary should be stated in the code so it doesn't get promoted later unnoticed.
MINOR:
  - The `verification` line previously carried the blocker summary text (`"; ".join(blockers)`); it now carries only counts. The human-quick-signal in the item's verification history is lost — the blocker detail now lives only in a multi-line evidence blob.
  - Comment claims the `data/backlog/**` exclusion covers "the derived backlog projections that `--apply` itself writes" — `--apply` writes item context via the API; the projections are written by `gen_backlog_summary.py`/`gen_docs_index.py`. Misleading provenance comment invites someone to "clean up" a justified exclusion.
  - `_latest_review` swallows all `json.loads`/stat exceptions silently (`except Exception: continue`), which can hide corrupt evidence and let the gate fall through to "no evidence" or pick an older file without any observability signal.
  - `_latest_review` returns `d` (parsed) but reads `fp.stat().st_mtime` twice and never checks the file's `sha` field against the filename, so filename/contents mismatch is undetected.
NIT:
  - The diff mixes unrelated concerns: id-block allocator churn for test scopes (`_test_staleness`, `_test_lease_gate`) and derived doc regeneration ride along with a gate-behavior change, hurting reviewability and bisectability.
  - `documentation-index.html` regains "no newline at end of file" on every generator run — a persistent, noisy one-line diff.
  - `review_block` recomputes the gate label from `mode` in three places (`review_block`, `_ingest`, `main`) — single source of truth for mode→gate mapping would be less brittle if a Gate 3 ever appears.
  - `gate` parser help/description is absent; the operator-facing hint about running `run --mode design` is only emitted in the failure path.
SUMMARY:
  - Verdict: does not yet satisfy the AC. Item-side storage is attempted but its API contract is unproven and non-idempotent, and the "gate sheet" half of the acceptance criterion has no implementation at all.
  - Top risks: (1) acceptance half-delivered; (2) gate exits 0 on BLOCKER findings — fails open; (3) stale, sha-unvalidated reviews presented as current; (4) over-broad `engineering/**` sha exclusion weakens review integrity; (5) mode-less evidence filenames overwrite each other.
  - Recommend: confirm the context API's evidence contract, fail-closed exit codes, sha freshness check, and an explicit gate-sheet write before this can be considered done.
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present
